facts.statement: Native defaults are block model, 64 rows by 64 columns, center block mapping, no layer file/grid-output filename, detailed3D off. These are defaults, not the effective TAP invocation.
Command-line options are read first; config-file options are appended and later duplicate names removed. CLI values therefore override the file, whose remaining values override initialized defaults.

The native HotSpot7 grid steady writer emits every layer as Layer n:, followed by zero-based row-major index i*cols+j and Kelvin at two decimals. Its top-layer comment is stale. This is grid-cell output, not block-mapped steady output.
The successor HotSpot7 grid writer has the same all-layer format. Its C file has separate macro-guarded material-coupling additions; whole-file byte equivalence with d250 is false.

Native HotSpot6 without SENTILAB_GRID_DUMP_ALL_LAYERS writes a headerless index/T_K grid and a blank line after each row. The selected silidx is 0 when secondary is off, 3 with secondary plus LCF, and 5 with secondary without LCF. It is not selected from the power-enabled flag. The captured TAP config has secondary off, so its native6 output is layer0 only.

SENTILAB_GRID_DUMP_ALL_LAYERS=1 selects a writer with Layer n: for every layer and an identifying marker. The build script produces hotspot-tap-faithful with SUPERLU=0 and hotspot with SUPERLU=1 plus this writer macro. The compiled identity and actual build have not been observed here.

With model_type=grid, the block-mapped steady dump names layer_n_unit, hsp_/hsink_ package units and inode_n peripheral nodes, with two-decimal Kelvin. The native6 main steady path prints Unit/Steady(Kelvin) and that dump to stdout; native7 writes the configured files and has no equivalent unconditional thermal stdout dump. Do not parse a grid file as this stream.

facts.scope: draft writer; also byte-identical in successor
facts.statement: The generator emits six explicit lateral-enabled LCF layers: substrate200um, C4/underfill70um, interposer110um, microbump/underfill10um, chip150um, TIM20um. Only layer4 enables power. The ptrace assigns configured powers only to Chiplet_*; other L4 units receive zero. Powered-layer status does not mean uniform power over the whole layer.

facts.scope: draft writer; also byte-identical in successor
facts.statement: Input die centres/sizes are mm; FLP dimensions and lower-left coordinates are metres. Die lower-left is centre/1000 minus half-size/1000. In L4, Chiplet and Ubump-named regions use silicon; Edge regions use bump mixture. L3 uses bump mixture for written die/halo/edge regions; fill_space adds whitespace with underfill properties. Names alone do not establish material.

facts.scope: draft detailed3D C; related successor separately pinned
facts.statement: For detailed3D, per-unit FLP resistivity and volumetric heat capacity override the layer fallback when present. L1/C4 and L2/interposer slabs carry calculated mixture properties in their FLPs. Resolve properties from the actual generated region and flags, not only LCF defaults.

With LCF and secondary off, the C model reads six LCF layers then appends two package layers: spreader6 and sink7; there is no second implicit TIM. They retain the TIM FLP extent and grid-to-block map. Detailed3D replaces the package block-to-grid map and clears its per-cell material override flags, so package properties come from spreader/sink configuration. Grid writers emit central cuboid cells, not peripheral inode values; package outlines can extend beyond that field domain.

facts.scope: draft writer; also byte-identical in successor
facts.statement: The generator only creates new_hotspot.config when it is absent. On that branch it sets spreader side=2*interposer and sink side=4*interposer (metres), and replaces r_convec with 0.1*0.06^2/sink_side^2 by exact template-line matching. Existing generated config is retained. Source alone does not prove an old run performed scaling; fixture comparisons need a fresh directory.

facts.statement: Both captured raw45mm reference configs declare sink0.18m, spreader0.09m, r_convec0.011111111111111112K/W, ambient318.15K, secondary0, block model, grid64x64 and center mapping. The invocation overrides model_type to grid and detailed3D on. These retained input bytes are not an observed effective runtime configuration.

facts.scope: draft warm worker; byte-identical in successor
facts.statement: tap_oracle_worker selects the requested binary and passes -c new_hotspot.config, -f sampleL4_ChipLayer.flp, -p sample.ptrace, steady/grid outputs, model_type grid, detailed3D on, the LCF, requested rows/cols, and grid_map_mode max. HotSpotOracle defaults rows/cols to32x32. The worker requires headers for all8 layers and returns layer4 as the heatmap. A HotSpot6Oracle uses this same worker after separate gate checks, so its search worker also forces max; its native6 gate-validation command is a different path.

slab049.tap_argv uses explicit binary/config/L4 FLP/ptrace/steady/grid/model grid/detailed3D/LCF arguments. For grid64 it leaves rows/cols and center mapping to the captured config; grid32 adds only rows/cols, preserving center mapping. reference_validation uses this argv with a private executable copy; its solver environment pins locale, zone and BLAS thread/dispatch settings. This code path has not run here.

Native grid-to-block center mapping uses the half-open mapped block bounds and averages four indexed terms; duplicated indices yield1,2or4distinct cells. Row0 is the top/north row. This observable differs from the active-layer grid peak/argmax and from a whole-dump maximum.

The record binds grid format to evaluator identity, obtains the single powered layer from LCF, requires complete block evidence, and records the literal stdout selector separately from its steady-file counterpart. For all-layer files it separately reports active-layer peak/argmax, weighted native centre mappings and same-index stack fields. For native6 macro-off it returns only the scoped layer0 grid and cannot derive the other grid layers from it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SLAB-049: build the HotSpot 6.0 evaluator, TAP-2.5D's HotSpot (uvahotspot/HotSpot a7a3286e), on x86_64 or
# aarch64 (Debian/Ubuntu; the same packages on amd64 and arm64):
#   apt-get install build-essential libsuperlu-dev libblas-dev
# Two binaries come from the vendored source in sundai_hotspot6/:
#   hotspot               the evaluator: SuperLU direct solver plus the all-layer grid dump
#                         (-DSENTILAB_GRID_DUMP_ALL_LAYERS=1, writer only; the solver is unchanged)
#   hotspot-tap-faithful  the cross-check: upstream source, SUPERLU=0, as TAP-2.5D's util/hotspot was built
# -ffp-contract=off stops GCC contracting a*b+c into one fused multiply-add in the HotSpot sources it compiles here
# (GCC contracts by default where the target has FMA, as aarch64 does; the x86_64 baseline target has none). It
# does not reach the precompiled SuperLU, BLAS or libm, which may pick FMA or other kernels per CPU. So it narrows
# cross-architecture differences; it does not make results bit-identical across architectures, and none is claimed.
# Binary hashes depend on the toolchain and, through the Makefile's -g, on the build path. Every host pins its own
# through gate zero: an aarch64 build needs its own receipts. sundai_hotspot.provenance writes
# <binary>.provenance.json for each binary (compiler, flags, build path, SuperLU/BLAS packages, the libraries the
# loader resolves with their hashes, the binary hash); validate-reference refuses a binary without it.

make cleano >/dev/null
rm -f hotspot hotspot-tap-faithful
make hotspot SUPERLU=0 EXTRAFLAGS="-ffp-contract=off"
mv hotspot hotspot-tap-faithful
make cleano >/dev/null
make hotspot SUPERLU=1 SUPERLULIB=-lsuperlu BLASLIB=-lblas SLU_HEADER="$SLU_HEADER" \
  EXTRAFLAGS="-DSENTILAB_GRID_DUMP_ALL_LAYERS=1 -ffp-contract=off"
make cleano >/dev/null
echo "architecture $arch"
gcc --version | head -n 1
sha256sum hotspot hotspot-tap-faithful
cd "$root"
python3 -m sundai_hotspot.provenance hotspot6 hotspot6_tap_faithful

def gen_ptrace(self, filename):
		num_component = 0
		component, component_name, component_index = [], [], []
		# Read components from flp file
		with open (self.path + filename + 'L4_ChipLayer.flp','r') as FLP:
			for line in FLP:
				line_sp = line.split()
				if line_sp:
					if line_sp[0] != '#':
						component.append(line_sp[0])
						comp = component[num_component].split('_')
						component_name.append(comp[0])
						component_index.append(int(comp[1]))
						num_component+=1	

		with open (self.path + filename + '.ptrace','w') as Ptrace:
			# Write ptrace header
			for i in range(0,num_component):
				# if component_name[i] == 'Core':
				Ptrace.write(component[i]+'\t')
			Ptrace.write('\n')
			for i in range(0,num_component):
				if component_name[i] == 'Chiplet':
					Ptrace.write(str(self.power[component_index[i]])+'\t')
				# elif component_name[i] == 'Ubump':
				# 	Ptrace.write('0.3\t')
				else:
					Ptrace.write('0\t')
			Ptrace.write('\n')
